purpose: Ablation of RESEARCH_LOG #13, run to try to REJECT it rather than extend it. #13 found the frozen composite ranks severe-loss risk monotonically and stably, but the worst decile was also the most volatile slice and carried the highest shadow-window return, which is what a pure volatility ranking would look like. This run adds every single-factor book and a plain twenty-session realised-volatility sort computed straight off the panel. If the free volatility sort ranks tail risk as well as the composite, #13 is not a finding and the forward record should be closed.
knownLimitations: This ablation was designed after seeing #13, so it carries selection exposure and can only REJECT the finding, never strengthen it.
Realised volatility is one free alternative among several; failing to beat it does not prove the composite is the only such alternative.
The single-factor books are compared after the fact, so the best of twelve is not a clean estimate of any one factor's standalone ranking power.
An exclusion screen is only useful against a universe that is otherwise being selected from; it produces no return on its own and this module measures no portfolio.
Excluding the worst bucket also removes whatever upside it contained, so the return excess of the excluded slice is reported alongside its severe-loss excess and must be read together.
Severe loss is defined on the executable gross return at the chosen horizon and ignores borrow, limit-locked exits and any impact beyond the frozen cost assumption.
Bucket boundaries are fixed deciles chosen before evaluation; a screen tuned to a different cut after seeing this run would carry selection exposure that these numbers do not price.
Every historical evaluation window has already been viewed, so this run can reject a screen but can never validate or promote one.
A stable historical tail ranking is not a guarantee of future tail behaviour, particularly across a regime change of the kind visible between these two windows.
